title: Removing Event Handlers
subtopics: Cleaning up handlers during component teardown
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of removing event handlers in a jQuery application.
Apply .off() in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify removing a specific handler with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through removing event handlers with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns .off() into a repeatable implementation choice. Use .on() for current event handling. Delegation allows a stable parent to handle events from future matching descendants, while event namespaces help cleanup.

Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.

content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for removing event handlers, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.text: Implement removing event handlers in a small interactive widget. Verify it works for keyboard input where appropriate and that handlers are not registered twice.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
summary: Removing Event Handlers is one part of the events and interaction workflow.
